cells.remarks: Issued from Murasi-sefjma. The writer was Kāyastha Kōighōha, the son of Vallabhaghōsha and the engraver was Mahāsandhivigrahin Malladatta, the son of Dhāradatta. In characters of about the tenth century. Published in J. P. A. cells.remarks: Issued from Vini(ni)tapura. Records the gift of land in the village Talakajja in the Sanulā-vishaya in the Kōsala country, to a brāhma named Kōmadēva, the son of Narasinha and the grandson of Harsha, who hailed from Māthila and was a resident of Jalajadda in Kōsala, and who belonged to Kāṣyapa-gōtra with the pravaras of Kāṣyapa, Vatsa and Naidhru[va] and was a student of the Vādaśa (Vījnsa)nōya-mādhyandina-sākhā. for the merit of his parents and of himself. The charter was composed by a person (name not given) who was the son of Allava and was known to Mahāsandhivigrahin Rūnaka Dhāradatta, in the presence of Uchohhavaṇga and was engraved by Vijñēnin Mūdhava, son of Vīsu. There is a supplementary portion referring to a Sōmavamśi king named Svabhāvatunga and probably to his conquest of Chēdi. Do. Published in J.P.A. S. B., Vol. I (1905), pp. 14 ff. See J. A. S., Letters, Vol. XIX (1953), pp. 117 ff. and Plates. See Bhandarkar's List, No. 1605.

cells.remarks: Records the construction of the step-well by Rājāmatī, the daughter of Bhairavadāsa who was the son of Uvāra, the son of Chhujjaio of Siraṅgagara. Gives the details of the lavish gifts and donations made by several Sultāns viz., Alauddin (Khalfjī) of Mālwā, Muzaffara Shāh of Gujarāt, Husain Shāh of Jaunpur, Barbak of Pānduä, Sultān (name not given) of Delhi (i.e. Delhi), Tughluq Shāh of… [name not given] and others, and of the gifts made by Sultān (name not given) of Vidara (i.e. Bidar) to Rājāmatī. Also mentions one of Rājāmatī's sons named Rānachandra who was a musician and a favourite of Sultāns Ghiyāsud-din and Muzaffar Shāh. The teacher of Rājāmatī and the musicians were Vu(Bu)rahāmata-su(suhukhu), Mīlā and others. The writer was Muni Guṇasundara.

Sēmantasītha is also stated to have built a big temple and installed in it an image of Pārīvanātha in front of the temple of Nēmi (i.e. Nēminātha) at the fort of the Raivata mountain. Also states that this minister provided the Rēvati-kuṇda at Dvāravati (i.e. Dvārakā) with a new flight of steps, for the welfare of his mother. He also caused to be made images of Mahēsa and Jalasāyin together with those of Gangēsa, Kshētrapāla, Arkka and Chandkikā as well as of Baladēva and Rēvati beeides constructing a well with araghaffa.
